findings.location: SPEC.md CAP-7 success; cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers (CAP-7) > Identical findings
findings.issue: CAP-7 success says the comparison key and fixture are in cell-contract.md, but cell-contract.md defines only the key (version, browser, scenario, step, action) and says 'on bankwire'. No fixture with a known blocking bug is defined. If bankwire is clean, both finding sets are empty and the test passes without exercising the sequential-confirmation path at all.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer has no failing fixture to build, so the identical-findings test can pass trivially. The rerun-seq / parallel_only logic ships unproven.
findings.suggestion: Define the fixture in cell-contract.md: e.g. a bankwire copy under scripts/tests/live/fixtures with one planted FO bug and one planted BO bug that fail on every engine, plus one scenario that fails only under concurrent DB writes. Assert non-empty, equal confirmed sets and a non-empty parallel_only for the interference case.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers (CAP-7) > Parallel-only failures; SPEC.md CAP-7 success ('findings are identical to a sequential run')
findings.issue: Sequential confirmation runs only for engines that have findings. Parallel interference can also hide a failure: engine A's BO scenario changes shared config (e.g. it disables the payment for a country, or empties the bank list) while engine B's FO scenario runs and passes only because of that change. Nothing reruns a passing engine, so the claim that findings are identical to a sequential run holds in one direction only.
findings.implementation_impact: A parallel tier-1 pass can be a false pass that a sequential run would have failed. That weakens the honesty law for gate-grade evidence, and the identical-findings test cannot catch it unless its fixture contains a masking case.
findings.suggestion: Either state the limitation and narrow the CAP-7 claim to 'no extra findings', or prevent masking: hold the cross-engine lock in shared mode for FO scenarios and exclusive mode for BO scenarios, so a BO scenario never overlaps any FO scenario of the other engine. Add a masking case to the fixture.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers (CAP-7), third bullet (BO login fallback)
findings.issue: When one engine's BO login fails while the other's succeeds, that engine 'reruns after the other finishes, sequentially'. Nothing says the DB is restored first or that `{browser}` is expanded differently. The first attempt already ran that engine's FO-only scenarios and wrote data keyed by `{browser}`, so the second attempt collides with its own leftovers (duplicate customer email, existing cart, address). The case where both engines fail BO login is also unspecified.
findings.implementation_impact: The fallback produces spurious findings, and these are not parallel-only, so they survive confirmation and become blocking. Behaviour when both logins fail is left to the implementer.
findings.suggestion: Make the login-fallback rerun restore the `snapshot-db` dump first (as rerun-seq does), or expand `{browser}` to `<engine>-retry`. Say which record and phase entry (`browser:<engine>#2`) replaces the first attempt. Specify that when both logins fail, BO steps stay inconclusive per today's rule with no rerun.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers (CAP-7) > Parallel-only failures (rerun-seq restore)
findings.issue: rerun-seq restores only the DB. Files the parallel pass wrote are kept: uploads, generated PDFs/invoices, module-written files under modules/<mod>, var/cache including class_index and Smarty compiles, and opcache. The warm reset deliberately clears these because DB-only resets leave residue. The two reset paths are inconsistent.
findings.implementation_impact: A failure caused by file or cache residue from the parallel pass can reproduce in rerun-seq and be confirmed as a blocking finding, or a cache built against the pre-restore DB can make the rerun flaky.
findings.suggestion: Reuse the warm `reset-files` (limited to var/cache plus files absent from a docroot list captured at `snapshot-db`) and `reset-opcache` steps before each `rerun-seq:<engine>`, or state explicitly why the DB restore alone is enough.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Warm container (CAP-5) > Teardown
findings.issue: ps-run-layer stops this owner's keepers 'before any run without --warm', which includes `cold-canary` for the same version as the keeper. The usual fix-loop sequence is warm pass, then cold-canary. When the cold-canary run fails (the case cold runs exist to catch, install-path bugs), the plan returns to `focus` with `e2e_warm` true, and a new keeper must pull, bring up and wait-healthy again. The slot cap (default 6) allows the keeper and the cold run to coexist.
findings.implementation_impact: Each failed promotion costs an extra full boot, which erodes the warm-loop savings exactly where iterations repeat.
findings.suggestion: Keep the keeper alive across `cold-canary` / `cold-version` runs of the same focus version. Stop it only when the focus cell's version changes, before `gate`, at loop end, or when slots are short.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Warm container (CAP-5) > Chain / Owner (owner token = session token)
findings.issue: The warm owner token is the validation session token, which is minted fresh on every psm-validate invocation. If Budi re-invokes psm-validate within the TTL (new conversation, or a restart after a crash), the previous keeper is foreign. It is never reused, and its stop needs Budi's OK. The 'at most one per (module, version, owner)' rule then allows a second keeper for the same module and version. Two keepers hold two slots, and the old one idles for up to 60 minutes.
findings.implementation_impact: There will be duplicate keepers, wasted slots and an extra cold boot per re-invocation. The On Activation listing turns into a recurring prompt that Budi must answer.
findings.suggestion: Add an adopt path: On Activation offers to re-own a keeper of the same module whose orchestrator session ended (rewrite owner in session.json under the lease) with one OK. Alternatively, stop keepers of the same module and dead orchestrator session without asking, and cap keepers per (module, version) at one regardless of owner.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Plan, definition of 'recorded failure' and step 7 `focus`
findings.issue: 'Recorded failure' = the newest conclusive record of any freshness has `state: fail`, with no session or age bound. A canary failure from a validation weeks ago, never re-run since because the module was then reworked, makes the first run of a new session a warm, failed-only run on an obsolete failed set. A mandatory cold-canary follows. On a now-clean module the canary version then boots three times (keeper, cold-canary, tier 1) instead of the two the Success signal promises.
findings.implementation_impact: The Success signal ('canary version boots twice' on a clean module) fails whenever the history holds an old failure, and the first iteration tests the wrong scenario subset.
findings.suggestion: Bound 'recorded failure' to records carrying the current `--session`. Otherwise the first focus run of a session is cold and full. Add a test: an old-session fail plus a new session derives a cold full `focus`.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Plan (rerun_matrix reason `not-gradeable` vs definition of a not-gradeable cell)
findings.issue: The rerun_matrix reason `not-gradeable` is defined as 'a gate-grade pass that is not passing gate-grade', which includes a pass with non-empty `inconclusive` or `browser_notes`. The step derivation defines a not-gradeable cell more narrowly: `authored_assertions` 0 or `scenario_notes` non-empty. Those cells count as passing for promotion. The same term thus names two different sets. A pass with inconclusive steps shows reason `not-gradeable` in rerun_matrix but blocks promotion and feeds `blocked-infra`.
findings.implementation_impact: Implementers and the orchestrator reading rerun_matrix will treat infra-flaky passes as structurally ungradeable, or the reverse. Tests written against one definition break against the other.
findings.suggestion: Split the reason: `not-gradeable` only for the step-derivation set, and `inconclusive-steps` / `browser-notes` (the existing blocked-infra cause names) for the rest.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Plan step 3 `blocked-infra`; tier-matrix.md Rules (inconclusive = infra cause)
findings.issue: The infra bucket includes causes that a module can produce: `install` (the module's install() throws or returns false on one version), and `inconclusive-steps` when the module breaks BO login so `bo_authed` is false and every BO step is inconclusive. Twice in a session, these become `blocked-infra`, which ends the E2E loop 'like skipped' and is reported as an infrastructure problem.
findings.implementation_impact: A real module defect can be labelled infra in the report. The orchestrator then tells Budi to fix Docker instead of the module, and the fix loop stops instead of sending the defect to psm-develop.
findings.suggestion: Keep the state rule, but have the report distinguish module-attributable causes (`install` with a module-side error, BO login failing only after the module is installed) from pure infra (`no-slots`, `crash`, `keeper-start`, pull/boot timeouts). Name the former 'blocked-module-suspect' or at least add a hint in `e2e_blocked_causes`.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Evidence record > Storage (append-only history, corrupt-history rule)
findings.issue: Appends are 'one write() under flock', but a writer killed mid-write (`--stop-job` escalates to SIGKILL after 60 s; WSL drvfs gives no atomicity for writes) can leave a final line without a trailing newline. The next append is then glued onto that partial line. The new, valid record becomes part of an unparsable line and is silently lost, and the cell stays `corrupt-history`.
findings.implementation_impact: A valid gate-grade record can disappear after any interrupted append, which forces a rerun and possibly a `blocked-infra` loop that is hard to diagnose.
findings.suggestion: Before appending, under the lock, check the last byte of the file. If it is not '\n', write '\n' first in the same write(). Add a test: a partial line without a newline followed by an append reads as one valid record.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Headless; Plan step 3 `blocked-infra`
findings.issue: A headless run returns at the first step that is not clean, so one call never produces two records for one cell in the same session. Each headless call also mints its own session. `blocked-infra` is therefore unreachable in headless mode. A headless caller (psm-develop / psm-cross-version fix loops) that re-calls psm-validate on `ready: false` will cold-boot the same infra-failing cell forever.
findings.implementation_impact: Under persistent infra failure (missing image, no slots), unbounded boot loops are possible through headless callers, and the return JSON gives callers no machine-readable signal to stop.
findings.suggestion: Either let headless callers pass a stable `--session` across their loop, or add to the headless return a per-cell `infra_cause` flag (`e2e_blocked_causes`-like) and specify in references/headless.md that callers must not retry on it.

findings.location: SPEC.md CAP-3; cell-contract.md > Runner > Fail-fast; Config keys `psm_e2e_slots` (default 6)
findings.issue: With the default 6 slots, tier 1 admits every version at once: 2 non-canary versions at cost 2, plus the canary version at cost 1, is 5 slots. Tier 0 steps are a single cell or a single version. Fail-fast therefore stops nothing in a default run unless other sessions occupy slots. The CAP-3 success test only shows it working with `--slots 1`. The test passes while the feature delivers no saving in the configuration Budi actually runs.
findings.implementation_impact: Not-run records, progress-log truncation and the sequential-fallback rule add complexity whose benefit cannot be seen in default runs, and the per-phase timing will not show any gain from it.
findings.suggestion: State the expected effect at default config, or make tier 1 admit versions in a defined order (oldest first, or the version with the most stale browsers first) with a staggered start (e.g. next version admitted only after the previous one reaches `browser:<engine>`), so fail-fast can save boots at default slots.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Warm container (CAP-5) > Reset per iteration; Evidence record > Fields (`reason` enumeration)
findings.issue: 'A failed reset or reload makes the iteration inconclusive', but `reset-db` / `reset-files` / `reset-opcache` failure is not in the `reason` enumeration. The fallback rule would classify it as `not-driven` or `errors` by accident. The same gap covers the `foreign-keeper`, `keeper-dead` and lease-held cold-boot fallbacks: they are logged, but nothing says whether the resulting record carries a marker.
findings.implementation_impact: Repeated reset failures cannot be told apart from module errors in `blocked-infra` causes or the report. Implementers will pick inconsistent reason strings.
findings.suggestion: Add reason `warm-reset` (with the failing sub-phase in `errors`) to the enumeration, and add an optional `boot_note` field (`foreign-keeper` | `keeper-dead` | `lease-held`) on cold-boot-fallback records.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > State, freshness, gate-grade > Fresh (`source_fingerprint` scope)
findings.issue: The fingerprint covers every file under the module directory except `.git/`, top-level `.psm-*` and `.memlog.md`. Editor and tool artefacts that PrestaShop never loads are included: vim `.*.swp`, `*~`, `.idea/`, `.vscode/`, `.DS_Store`, `.php-cs-fixer.cache`, `.phpunit.result.cache`. Opening a file in an editor during or after a run changes the fingerprint and stales every cell of every version. It also stays ambiguous whether `.memlog.md` is excluded only at top level.
findings.implementation_impact: Gate-grade evidence can be invalidated spuriously, forcing a full re-run of tier 0 and tier 1 (hours) for a change that cannot affect behaviour.
findings.suggestion: Add a fixed exclusion list of known non-runtime artefacts (editor swap/backup files, IDE folders, OS metadata, tool caches), applied at any depth. Keep `vendor/` and `tests/e2e` included. State that `.memlog.md` is top-level only, or that it applies at any depth. Add a test: creating `.foo.php.swp` leaves cells fresh.

findings.location: cell-contract.md:109 (Warm container > Reset per iteration) with cell-contract.md:87 (Plan step 7)
findings.issue: A failed reset-db/reset-files/reset-opcache says the warm container is discarded and 'the next run boots cold', but the next plan call still derives step 7 with a recorded failure, so e2e_warm is true and the orchestrator passes --warm again. Nothing records that the reset failed or forces a cold run. The inconclusive record's reason for a reset failure is also not named in the reason list.
findings.implementation_impact: ps-run-layer just starts a new keeper, which is a warm boot and not the promised cold run. On an image where reset-opcache can never succeed (an --extra-tag-map tag with neither php-fpm nor apachectl), warm iterations alternate between new keepers and reset failures. Implementers will guess the reason value, and blocked-infra matching depends on it.
findings.suggestion: Name a reason (e.g. 'warm-reset') for a reset failure. State the mechanism: either the plan emits e2e_warm=false when the focus cell's newest record has reason warm-reset, or ps-run-layer runs that iteration as a cold-boot fallback. State whether the first iteration on a fresh keeper runs the reset at all.

findings.location: cell-contract.md:103 (Warm container > Chain) with cell-contract.md:83 (Plan step 3 blocked-infra)
findings.issue: When the keeper exits before writing session.json, the cell gets inconclusive reason keeper-start, and there is no cold-boot fallback (unlike foreign-keeper, lease-held, keeper-dead and mismatch). The next derivation is again a focus step with e2e_warm true, so it retries the keeper. Two keeper-start records in one session trigger blocked-infra.
findings.implementation_impact: A defect that is specific to the keeper path (detach, session-file write, label stamping) ends the whole E2E loop with ready=false, even though an ordinary cold run of the focus cell would work. The operator gets no fix-loop feedback at all.
findings.suggestion: Specify that after a keeper-start record on the current fingerprint, the next focus run is a cold-boot fallback (or the plan sets e2e_warm=false). Alternatively, exclude keeper-start from the blocked-infra causes while a cold fallback is still possible.

findings.location: cell-contract.md:103-105 (Warm container > Chain / ownership)
findings.issue: Two statements conflict when a live keeper with another owner token exists for (module path, V): 'finds this owner's live keeper ... or starts one' and 'A keeper with another owner ... the iteration cold-boots and logs foreign-keeper'. This includes Budi's own keeper from an earlier psm-validate invocation, because each invocation mints a new session token.
findings.implementation_impact: One implementation starts a second keeper (two containers for the same module and version, both holding slots). Another permanently degrades every iteration of this session to cold boots until the foreign keeper's TTL expires. When the operator simply re-invokes the skill, the previous keeper is never reused or stopped and keeps a slot for up to 60 minutes.
findings.suggestion: State whether ps-run-layer starts its own keeper when a foreign keeper exists for the same (module, V), and how the orchestrator handles keepers left by its own previous invocation. For example, list them at On Activation with a default offer to stop them, or key ownership on something that persists across invocations.

findings.location: cell-contract.md:65 (State, freshness > Fresh)
findings.issue: The fingerprint covers every file under the module directory except .git/, top-level .psm-* and .memlog.md. It does not exclude psm_reports_dir, the screenshot dir, the headless config copy, or progress logs when these resolve inside the module directory. The default {project-root}/_bmad-output/psm-validate is inside the module whenever the module repo is the project root.
findings.implementation_impact: Each run's own history append, screenshot, or progress-log write changes the fingerprint. Every record is stale as soon as it is written, so no cell can ever reach gate-grade, and the plan loops on rerun with ready permanently false.
findings.suggestion: Exclude psm_reports_dir, the screenshot base and _bmad-output (resolved, when under the module dir) from the fingerprint walk, or make it an input error (exit 2) when the reports dir lies inside the module directory. Add a test that writes a history line under such a layout and the cell stays fresh.

findings.location: cell-contract.md:65 (State, freshness > Fresh)
findings.issue: The fingerprint walk takes (path, size, mtime_ns) for every file, but the spec does not say what happens when a file cannot be stat'ed: a broken symlink, a permission-denied file, or a file deleted between listing and stat. It also does not say whether symlinks are followed.
findings.implementation_impact: ps-run-layer, plan and aggregate may each crash, skip the file, or hash differently. Divergent results would make plan and aggregate disagree on freshness, or make the run fail before admission without writing a record.
findings.suggestion: Specify a single shared fingerprint function: use lstat and do not follow symlinks (hash the link target string). An unreadable entry is either included as a fixed marker or is an input error (exit 2) naming the path. Plan, runner and aggregate import the same function.

findings.location: cell-contract.md:80 (Plan > not-gradeable) and cell-contract.md:82 (step 2 blocked-not-gradeable)
findings.issue: Not-gradeable assumes that non-empty scenario_notes 'cannot change on the same fingerprint'. But scenario_notes include the deleted_specs notes from git status. Committing a spec deletion changes only .git/, which the fingerprint excludes, so the notes disappear while the fingerprint stays the same.
findings.implementation_impact: After the operator commits the deletion as the notes instruct, the plan still derives blocked-not-gradeable from the old record and runs nothing. The cell cannot be re-proved until some unrelated file is touched, and ready stays false for no current reason.
findings.suggestion: Treat a not-gradeable record as re-runnable when the current e2e_scenario_notes (computed by the plan before any boot) differ from the record's scenario_notes. Alternatively, include the git-derived deleted-spec list in the fingerprint input.

findings.location: tier-matrix.md:22 (Visual review) and tier-matrix.md:20 (Layer 3 respawn after loop-back)
findings.issue: Visual review now runs on the cold canary run inside Phase 1 and on cold-version/cold-canary after a loop-back. It read-merges into <module>-adversarial.json, which updates that file's mtime. The plan judges Layer 3 freshness by file mtime versus the newest source mtime plus the versions list.
findings.implementation_impact: A visual-review write made after the latest patch makes adversarial.json look fresh. At Phase 2 start, plan_layer reports adversarial as reuse, so the Layer 3 lenses are not respawned for the patched source. This contradicts the rule that Layer 3 output from before the new patch is stale and must be spawned again.
findings.suggestion: Specify that visual-review writes do not refresh Layer 3 freshness. For example, keep a separate lens timestamp or a source_fingerprint field in adversarial.json written only by the lenses, and have the plan compare that instead of the file mtime. Alternatively, defer visual-review writes until after the lenses are merged in Phase 2.

findings.location: tier-matrix.md:20 (tier 0 hosting loop) with cell-contract.md:89 (Plan > Phase 1)
findings.issue: The tier 0 host is 'the focus cell's version's loop' after a loop-back, and the hosting loop ends only on gate/done/an ending step. The spec does not say what happens when the focus cell changes version while tier 0 is in progress: cold-canary fails (focus becomes the canary), or a second failing cell from the same tier-1 run is at another version.
findings.implementation_impact: The orchestrator cannot tell whether V's loop keeps hosting the new focus, or whether it must end V's loop (which is not allowed before gate/done) and open the new version's loop. One reading leaves the new focus version's Layers 1/2/5 ungated by its own loop. The other has no defined exit condition for V's loop.
findings.suggestion: State that the hosting loop is fixed at loop-back entry and keeps hosting every tier-0 step until gate/done/an ending step. Or state that when e2e_focus_cell's version changes, the current loop ends after phase1_reuse is true for its version and the new focus version's loop takes over. Add a test for cold-canary failing inside a loop-back hosted in 8.1.

findings.location: cell-contract.md:129 (Parallel browsers > engine workers)
findings.issue: The version process reads each worker's result from the worker's output file. The spec does not cover a worker that crashes, is OOM-killed, hangs past its step timeouts, or leaves a missing or unparsable output file while the other worker succeeds. ps-run-layer writes a crash record only when the child (the version process) left no result.
findings.implementation_impact: The version process returns a result for one engine only. The other cell gets no record, or a pass/fail record with null fields (read as incomplete-record), depending on the implementation. A hung worker blocks teardown indefinitely, because no worker-level timeout is defined.
findings.suggestion: Specify that a worker with no valid output file gets an inconclusive cell inside the version result (reason crash, browser_notes naming the worker exit code). Add a worker wall-clock bound (e.g. derived from scenario count × step timeouts) after which the version process kills it and records the same.

findings.location: cell-contract.md:131 (Parallel browsers > BO login fallback)
findings.issue: When one engine's BO login fails and the other's succeeds, the failing engine reruns sequentially afterwards. The spec does not say what happens to the first parallel attempt's results, screenshots and console errors (kept, merged or discarded), what browser_mode the cell records, or whether the parallel-only rule (rerun-seq on a restored DB) applies to findings from this sequential rerun. It also does not say whether the DB is restored to the snapshot before the rerun, or what happens when both logins fail or the sequential rerun's login fails again.
findings.implementation_impact: Findings from the first, unauthenticated pass may be double-counted or lost. The fallback rerun runs against a DB already mutated by both parallel passes, so it can report state-caused failures that a sequential run would not. browser_mode does not reflect how the cell was actually driven.
findings.suggestion: Define the fallback: discard the first attempt's results for that engine, restore the snapshot-db dump before the rerun, record browser_mode as sequential for that cell, and exempt its findings from rerun-seq. If the login fails again, keep the inconclusive BO steps as today.

findings.location: cell-contract.md:45 (normalizer accepts webkit) with cell-contract.md:98, 130, 133 (fail-fast pair, lock, slots)
findings.issue: The normalizer accepts chromium/firefox/webkit, so psm_e2e_browsers may hold three engines. Slots, parallel mode and fail-fast are specified only for two: 'a version that drives two browsers at cost 2', 'the second engine of a CAP-7 pair', 'does not start the second engine'.
findings.implementation_impact: With three browsers per version, the admission cost (3, or 2+1), the fallback when only two slots are free, whether all three workers run in parallel, and which engines get not-run after a fail-fast in sequential mode are all undefined. Implementations will diverge, and the slot cap can be exceeded or under-used.
findings.suggestion: Generalise: cost = number of engines driven concurrently. Admit at full cost when that many slots are free, else at cost 1 with --sequential-browsers. In sequential mode, every engine after the first fail gets not-run. Alternatively, restrict psm_e2e_browsers to at most two engines (exit 2).

findings.location: cell-contract.md:123 (Scenario prerequisites > duplicate names)
findings.issue: The spec says 'a spec whose effective name equals another spec's ... is skipped with a note naming both files', but does not say whether both colliding specs are skipped or only one, and if only one, which (first or later in file-name order).
findings.implementation_impact: Depending on the choice, a scenario named in another spec's requires may or may not survive. That changes which dependents are skipped transitively, the full scenario set, and the failed-only selection. Plan and runner could disagree if they are implemented separately.
findings.suggestion: State the rule explicitly. For example, all specs sharing an effective name are skipped (each note names every file in the collision), and dependents of that name are skipped too. Add a test with two files that share a name.

findings.location: cell-contract.md:51 (Evidence record > Storage, append and corrupt-history)
findings.issue: Each append is one write() under flock, but a short or interrupted write (ENOSPC, kill during write) can leave a final line without a trailing newline. The next append then lands on the same physical line.
findings.implementation_impact: The next valid record is merged into the corrupt line and silently lost. The cell keeps reason corrupt-history until yet another record is written, so one infra hiccup costs an extra full cold run of that cell.
findings.suggestion: Before appending under the flock, check whether the file's last byte is a newline and write one first if it is not. Verify that the write returned the full length, and treat a short write as an append failure that ps-run-layer reports.

findings.location: cell-contract.md:162 (Headless > return JSON, 'not reached')
findings.issue: 'A cell the run never reached gets reason not reached: stopped at <step>' does not define 'reached'. A cell may have no record from this call but carry older records (stale, or fresh from an earlier session) whose aggregate reason is missing/stale-source/fail/not-run.
findings.implementation_impact: The headless caller may receive 'not reached' for a cell that holds a current fresh fail from a previous run, which hides a real blocking finding. Or it may receive the stale aggregate reason for a cell this call never touched. Either way, the per-version verdict contract is ambiguous.
findings.suggestion: Define 'reached' as: the cell has a record with this call's --session. For unreached cells, report 'not reached: stopped at <step>' and also keep the aggregate's state and reason in separate fields, so that an existing fresh fail is never masked.

findings.location: cell-contract.md:51 (history path <module>-e2e-<ver>-<browser>.jsonl) with cell-contract.md:80 (failing uses fresh or stale records)
findings.issue: Cell histories are keyed by the module name only, and records carry no module path. The plan's failing, focus-cell, recorded-failure and step-6 stale-pass rules deliberately use stale records. So records written by another copy of the same module (a different path, worktree or fork in the same reports dir) count as this module's history.
findings.implementation_impact: A cold fail recorded for another copy makes a cell 'failing' here. It can become the focus cell, block cold-canary and gate, or trigger warm/failed-only runs on scenarios that never failed for this source. A stale pass from the other copy can promote cold-canary.
findings.suggestion: Add a module_path (resolved absolute path) field to every record, and ignore records whose module_path differs from the current module in plan and aggregate. Alternatively, key the history file name on a hash of the module path.

findings.location: tier-matrix.md > Visual review; cell-contract.md > Plan > Phase 1; SKILL.md Lapis 3/4; ps-plan-layers.py plan_layer (adversarial reuse = file mtime newer than newest source)
findings.issue: Visual review now happens in Phase 1: the cold canary run, and after a loop-back the cold-version and cold-canary runs. A blocking visual defect is read-merged into <module>-adversarial.json, which rewrites the file and gives it an mtime newer than the source. The plan decides whether Layer 3 reruns by that mtime alone (provenance None). So once a visual defect is written in Phase 1, the Phase 2 plan reports adversarial `reuse`, and the four lenses never spawn for the current source. This happens on a first validation with no prior review, and after a loop-back it leaves pre-patch lens output in place. Today it cannot happen, because visual review runs only after Layer 3 has spawned in Phase 2.
findings.implementation_impact: If the developer follows the tier-matrix literally, a module can reach the aggregate with Layer 3 never run, or with Layer 3 run on an older source, and adversarial still reads as fresh. That is a silent honesty-law breach.
findings.suggestion: Pick one and state it. Option A: defer writing visual defects until after the Layer 3 merge in Phase 2, holding Phase 1 judgments in a scratch file. Option B: give adversarial freshness a provenance field (e.g. the source_fingerprint the lenses reviewed) so a visual-only write cannot refresh it. Add a test: write a visual defect after a patch, then check that the plan still marks adversarial rerun.

findings.location: tier-matrix.md > Rules (loop-back re-enters Phase 1, Layer 3 'is spawned again'); SKILL.md Lapis 3/4 read-merge; references/run-phases.md read-merge rule
findings.issue: Under the read-merge rule, every write to adversarial.json keeps the existing findings and appends to them. With loop-backs Phase 2 can run several times, yet the contract never says what happens to findings from earlier Layer 3 rounds or earlier visual reviews once a patch fixes them. Respawned lenses merge on top of the stale findings and duplicate them. A visual defect that was fixed keeps blocking `ready`.
findings.implementation_impact: After any loop-back, `ready` can stay false forever on findings that were already fixed. Otherwise the developer has to invent a purge rule that the read-merge contract forbids.
findings.suggestion: Define the lifecycle. For example: on Layer 3 respawn, replace the lens-sourced findings while keeping visual ones, and tag visual findings with the source_fingerprint/run they came from so a later cold full run of that cell can retire them. Or state that the orchestrator rewrites the file from scratch after a patch, and say which findings survive.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Plan > Phase 2 entry; > Plan (phase1_reuse 'emitted in both modes'); references/run-phases.md Fase 1/2
findings.issue: The Phase 2 entry check is 'one plan call with the run scope must show phase1_reuse true', but the contract does not say whether that call runs in per-version or canonical mode. In canonical mode, static/flashlight/scenario are judged against <module>-<layer>.json, which only Phase 2's merge-only and cross-version static scan write. In canonical mode phase1_reuse is therefore false before Phase 2 starts, so Phase 2 can never start. In per-version mode it works.
findings.implementation_impact: A developer who picks canonical mode deadlocks the Phase 1 to Phase 2 transition.
findings.suggestion: State that the Phase 2 entry call (and every phase1_reuse read) uses `--per-version` with the run-scope `--versions`. Add a test: all per-version files fresh and no canonical files gives phase1_reuse true.

findings.location: tier-matrix.md > Rules (tier 0 hosted in canary version's loop, 'after a loop-back, of the focus cell's version'); cell-contract.md > Plan > Phase 1 (test: loop-back hosted in 8.1 derives cold-canary)
findings.issue: Which Phase 1 loop hosts tier 0 is stated in terms of 'after a loop-back', but no plan field says whether a loop-back is in progress, and the plan's e2e_focus_cell changes as steps advance. At cold-canary the plan reports the canary as focus, yet the test says 8.1 still hosts. With two failing cells the focus moves to another version mid-loop. At session start, a stale failing cell from an earlier session already makes the plan derive `focus` on a non-canary cell (`failing` counts stale records). There the orchestrator cannot tell whether it is 'after a loop-back', and the canary is not run first even though Budi asked for 9 + Chrome first.
findings.implementation_impact: The orchestrator (an LLM) has to judge which loop hosts the E2E step and when it ends, which violates the 'never picks a tier by judgment' rule. The hosting loop's exit condition (phase1_reuse for *its* version) depends on that guess.
findings.suggestion: Have the plan emit `e2e_host_version`, derived from records (e.g. the version of the cell whose failure opened the current loop-back, else the canary version). State explicitly that a stale failing cell from an earlier session starts a loop-back on that cell instead of the canary, or give the canary priority at session start.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Plan > Phase 1; tier-matrix.md tier 0 'Starts when: every patch, inside the Phase 1 loop'
findings.issue: Inside the hosting version's Phase 1 iteration, the order of Layers 1/2/5 and the E2E step is unspecified. Can the E2E step boot while that version's Layer 2 (install) is still failing or stale, or only after Layers 1/2/5 are clean for that version?
findings.implementation_impact: One developer runs E2E every iteration and burns cold boots whose install failure is already known from Layer 2, producing inconclusive 'install' records that count toward blocked-infra. Another waits. The behaviour and the boot counts in the success signal differ.
findings.suggestion: State the order. For example: in the hosting loop, run the E2E step only when that version's phase1_reuse is true (or at least when flashlight is not failing). Otherwise patch Layers 1/2/5 first.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Configured cells / Aggregate / Headless ('ready and versions cover exactly the caller's cells'); ps-aggregate.py main (target_versions = --versions or static's versions; unscanned gate)
findings.issue: Today the aggregate's version set comes from `--versions` or the static scan's versions, not from psm_target_versions. The contract makes `--config` the only source of the configured E2E cells and says `versions` covers exactly the configured set. It does not say whether target_versions must now come from the config, what happens when the static scan (or `--versions`) covers fewer versions than the config (interactive narrowed scope), or whether a configured version absent from the static scan is an error.
findings.implementation_impact: When the static scan is narrowed, `versions[ver].e2e_state` can be missing for configured versions while `e2e_cells` lists them. Per-version `ready`, which headless callers read for 1.7/8/9, then silently omits versions.
findings.suggestion: State that the aggregate's target_versions = the configured psm_target_versions, and that a configured version missing from the static scan exits 2 (or is reported not-ready with a reason). Also say how `--versions` on the aggregate interacts with it.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Runner (`--cells <ver>:<browser>[+<browser>]` passes each version its own browser list) + Config keys (`--config` forwarded to children); ps-flashlight-run.py apply_config_file (explicit = value differs from parser default) and CONFIG_KEY_TO_DEST (psm_e2e_browsers -> browsers)
findings.issue: ps-run-layer has to tell each child which browsers to drive, and it also forwards `--config`. The child's apply_config_file treats a flag whose value equals the parser default as 'not given' and overwrites it from the config. A child asked for exactly `chromium,firefox` (== DEFAULT_BROWSERS) under a config with psm_e2e_browsers `chromium,firefox,webkit` would also drive webkit: an unrequested cell, admitted at the wrong slot cost. The contract never says how the per-version browser list reaches the child.
findings.implementation_impact: This is a latent bug: extra or reordered engines are driven in a version child, records appear for cells the plan did not ask for, and slot accounting goes wrong.
findings.suggestion: Specify a dedicated child flag for the cell list (e.g. `--engines`, outside CONFIG_KEY_TO_DEST), or state that ps-run-layer does not forward `psm_e2e_browsers` to children. Add a test with config browsers ≠ default.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Configured cells (normalizer accepts webkit) vs > Parallel browsers / Slots / not-run / sequential fallback
findings.issue: webkit is a valid configured engine, so a version can need three browsers. CAP-7 is written for two: 'admits a version that drives two browsers at cost 2 ... otherwise cost 1', 'after both workers finish', 'the second engine of a version whose first engine fails gets not-run'. Nothing covers three engines: is the cost 3, can some engines run in parallel and the rest sequentially, and does the third engine get not-run after a sequential failure?
findings.implementation_impact: Implementations will differ on slot cost and fail-fast for any 3-browser config, and the slot cap can be exceeded.
findings.suggestion: Either generalise: cost = number of concurrently driven engines; when fewer slots are free, run with min(free, n) workers or fully sequential; in sequential mode, after a fail every later engine gets not-run. Or restrict CAP-7 parallelism to two engines and state what happens with more.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Warm container > Chain / Attach (`--warm`, `--use-warm <warm-id|auto>`, `--keep-warm`)
findings.issue: Which script owns each flag is unclear. Chain says the orchestrator passes `--warm --warm-owner` to ps-run-layer, which 'runs the child with `--use-warm <warm-id>`'. Attach then describes `--use-warm <warm-id|auto>` with `auto` lookup as if ps-run-layer accepts it and takes the lease. The format of the keeper's warm Job ID (it must pass valid_job_id and be distinguishable in `--list-jobs`) is also not given.
findings.implementation_impact: The developer has to guess the CLI surface of two scripts, and tests and docs (run-phases update) cannot be written against a fixed interface.
findings.suggestion: List each new flag with its owning script, e.g. ps-run-layer: `--warm`, `--warm-owner`; ps-e2e-run: `--keep-warm`, `--warm-ttl`, `--use-warm <warm-id>`. Say whether `auto` exists and where. Give the warm Job ID form (e.g. `<module>-e2e-warm-<HHMM>-<hex>`).

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Warm container > Chain vs 'At most one keeper per (module path, version, owner token). A keeper with another owner is never attached ... the iteration cold-boots and logs foreign-keeper'
findings.issue: These two rules give different outcomes when a keeper with another owner token is live for the same module and version. Chain says: find *this owner's* keeper or start one (there is none for this owner, so start a second keeper). The foreign-keeper rule says the iteration cold-boots. A common case: Budi re-invokes psm-validate in a new conversation, which mints a new session/owner token. His own keeper from the earlier session is now 'foreign', and unless he approves a stop, every warm iteration either falls back to cold or a second keeper starts alongside the first and takes another slot.
findings.implementation_impact: Either CAP-5 is defeated for up to the TTL after every re-activation, or the module and version get two containers. Which one depends on the developer's reading.
findings.suggestion: Pick one: e.g. 'a foreign keeper for the same (module, version) does not prevent starting this owner's keeper (cost 1 more slot)', or 'cold-boot fallback while any foreign keeper exists'. Consider also letting On Activation offer to stop the same user's previous-session keepers.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Warm container > Reset per iteration ('A failed reset or reload makes the iteration inconclusive, discards the warm container, and the next run boots cold') vs > Plan step 7 (e2e_warm true) and > Evidence record reason list
findings.issue: A failed reset has no `reason` among those enumerated (crash, stopped, browser-unavailable, keeper-start, no-slots, parallel-unconfirmed, incomplete-record, not-driven, errors, install, launch-error), so the developer has to guess (`errors`?). 'The next run boots cold' has no mechanism either: the plan still emits e2e_warm true, so the orchestrator passes `--warm` again and ps-run-layer starts a new keeper. If the reset failure is deterministic (e.g. no php-fpm master and no apachectl on a tag), every warm iteration fails the same way, and after two of them blocked-infra ends the whole E2E loop, even though a plain cold run would work.
findings.implementation_impact: There is no defined reason value. The 'boots cold' promise cannot be implemented as written, and a deterministic reset failure turns into a premature blocked-infra.
findings.suggestion: Add a reason (e.g. `warm-reset`). Define the fallback: either ps-run-layer falls back to a cold-boot run of the same cell when the keeper's reset fails (and records that), or the plan sets e2e_warm false when the focus cell's newest record has reason `warm-reset`. Exclude `warm-reset` from blocked-infra, or define how it counts.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Config keys > psm_e2e_slots (admission 'also counts the claims it already admitted whose container is not running yet: ps-run-layer records them in its own registry entry')
findings.issue: It is unclear whether one ps-run-layer process counts the pending claims of *other* ps-run-layer processes on the same host and temp dir, which it could read from their registry entries. The text says 'the claims it already admitted' (its own), yet the shared `slots.lock` flock and the sentence 'a claim from another temp dir becomes visible only once its container runs' imply that same-temp-dir claims from other processes are visible.
findings.implementation_impact: If only own claims are counted, two concurrent sessions on one host can each claim the last free slots during the long `pull`/`bring-up` window (up to 900 s+), and the cap is breached on exactly the saturation path it exists for.
findings.suggestion: State that admission sums `psm.slots` on running containers plus the `slot_claims` of every live ps-run-layer registry entry in `<tmp>/psm-jobs/` (entry_state alive), minus claims whose `psm.run` container already runs. Add a two-process test.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Plan (rerun_matrix reasons: '... then by the newest fresh record: fail, not-run, inconclusive, warm-only, partial, not-gradeable') vs > State, freshness, gate-grade ('has passing gate-grade evidence only when its newest gate-grade record is passing')
findings.issue: rerun_matrix picks its reason from the newest *fresh* record, but passing gate-grade evidence is judged from the newest *gate-grade* record. When a cell has a fresh passing gate-grade record followed by a newer non-gate-grade record on the same fingerprint, rerun_matrix lists it as `not-run`/`inconclusive`/`warm-only` (rerun), while `ready` and the derivation treat it as passing. This happens when cold-version re-drives a sibling browser that already passed and the sibling then gets no-slots or not-run, or after a flaky warm pass without a patch.
findings.implementation_impact: The plan and aggregate can contradict each other (`rerun` lists e2e while the step is `done` and `ready` is true). Tests written against one rule fail against the other.
findings.suggestion: Put 'has passing gate-grade evidence → no rerun entry' before the newest-fresh-record reasons. Or state explicitly that rerun_matrix is informational and may list cells that do not block.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Plan: rerun_matrix reason `not-gradeable` ('gate-grade pass that is not passing gate-grade') vs the derivation's definition of not-gradeable (authored_assertions 0 or scenario_notes non-empty, with empty inconclusive) and blocked-infra causes (inconclusive-steps, browser-notes)
findings.issue: One word has two meanings. In rerun_matrix, `not-gradeable` also covers a pass with inconclusive steps or browser_notes. In the derivation and in `e2e_blocked_causes`, such a cell is *not* not-gradeable: it is retried and can become blocked-infra.
findings.implementation_impact: Reports and tests that join rerun_matrix reasons with e2e_blocked_causes or the derivation will disagree, and the developer has to pick which definition the shared helper implements.
findings.suggestion: Split the reason: e.g. `not-gradeable` (narrow definition) vs `inconclusive-steps` / `browser-notes` for the retryable cases, and use the same names as the blocked-infra causes.

findings.location: tier-matrix.md > Rules ('An inconclusive cell (boot timeout, missing image, install failure, launch error, BO login failure)') vs cell-contract.md > State
findings.issue: The tier-matrix lists 'BO login failure' as making a cell inconclusive. Under the state rules a failed BO login only makes individual BO steps inconclusive (per-step conclusiveness unchanged), so the cell is `pass` with non-empty `inconclusive` or `fail`, never state `inconclusive`. The two documents disagree on the cell state.
findings.implementation_impact: One developer adds `bo_authed=false` as a cell-level inconclusive rule and another does not. The result changes whether a BO-login outage is retried as infra or reported as `inconclusive-steps`, and how blocked-infra fires.
findings.suggestion: Remove 'BO login failure' from the tier-matrix list, or reword it as 'a pass with inconclusive steps (e.g. BO login failure)'. Keep cell-contract's state rules as the single definition.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers ('when one engine's BO login fails while the other's succeeded, that engine reruns after the other finishes, sequentially')
findings.issue: The fallback is underspecified. _bo_login runs at the start of _drive_page and the worker then keeps running every scenario with bo_authed false. Should the worker abort right after a failed login, or finish and then rerun everything? Which results are kept: the first pass discarded, or merged? Does `browser_mode` stay `parallel`? Does the sequential rerun hold the BO lock, and how does it relate to the later `rerun-seq:<engine>` confirmation step?
findings.implementation_impact: The developer has to invent the control flow and the result-merging rule for a path that directly affects findings and `inconclusive`. Two implementations would produce different records.
findings.suggestion: Spell it out: e.g. 'a worker whose login fails stops before its first scenario and exits with `login-failed`. The version process runs that engine again alone after the other worker exits (phase `browser:<engine>#2`) and uses only the second pass. browser_mode stays `parallel`. rerun-seq applies afterwards as usual.'

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Evidence record > reason ('first state-rule cause that applies: not-driven, errors, install, launch-error') and > Plan step 3 blocked-infra ('same infra cause'); ps-e2e-run.py run_one_version (install failures append to res['errors'])
findings.issue: In today's runner, every install failure also appends a message to `errors`. Because `errors` is checked before `install`, reason `install` can never be produced. All version-level infra failures (missing image, pull error, wait-healthy timeout, install failure, wait-http failure) collapse into one reason, `errors`. blocked-infra then treats two *different* infra failures in one session as 'the same cause'.
findings.implementation_impact: blocked-infra can fire after a boot timeout followed by an image-missing error, ending the E2E loop on a coincidence. The `install` reason in the contract is dead code.
findings.suggestion: Either stop the runner from copying install failures into `errors` (so `install` is reachable), or define finer infra causes (e.g. `image-missing`, `boot-timeout`, `install`, `http-unreachable`) as the `reason` and compare those in blocked-infra.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Plan ('not-gradeable ... which a rerun on the same fingerprint cannot change'); ps-e2e-run.py deleted_specs (git status of tests/e2e)
findings.issue: The claim does not hold. scenario_notes include 'spec deleted from the working tree but still tracked by git', which comes from `git status`, and `.git/` is excluded from the fingerprint. The note itself tells the operator to commit the deletion. Committing it removes the note without changing the fingerprint, yet the plan stays at blocked-not-gradeable, because that step has no session or retry condition and the newest gate-grade record still carries the old note.
findings.implementation_impact: The plan is stuck until the operator touches an unrelated file just to change the fingerprint, which is a surprising dead end.
findings.suggestion: Compare the record's scenario_notes with the plan's current `e2e_scenario_notes` (already computed before any boot), and treat a mismatch as stale (rerun). Or include the git-tracked spec list (or HEAD) in the fingerprint.

findings.location: SPEC.md > Success signal ('CAP-6 timings show both'); cell-contract.md > Phase timings / Aggregate ('e2e_phase_durations ... from the records it actually used for the verdict')
findings.issue: The aggregate surfaces timings only from the records it selected (normally cold gate-grade ones). A warm fix-loop iteration is never selected once a gate-grade record exists, so the aggregate cannot show the warm iteration's timings that the success signal needs. Where the operator or a test should read the warm-vs-cold comparison is not stated.
findings.implementation_impact: The success signal cannot be checked from the documented output. The developer has to guess whether to add a history/timing report or to assert directly on the .jsonl.
findings.suggestion: State where the success signal is read: e.g. 'from the cell history `phase_durations`/`boot_phases`', or add a plan/aggregate field such as `e2e_last_runs` with per-run timings, including warm ones.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Config keys ('`--config` joins RESERVED_PASSTHROUGH; ps-run-layer forwards it to its children itself'); ps-run-layer.py docstring/main (Layers 2/5 receive flags after `--`)
findings.issue: Today, Layers 2 and 5 receive `--config` through the passthrough (`-- --config …`). After `--config` joins RESERVED_PASSTHROUGH, that form exits 2 for *every* layer, not just e2e. The contract describes ps-run-layer's `--config` handling only for E2E keys. It does not say whether Layer 2/5 children still receive the forwarded file, or whether `--config` should still map `psm_target_versions` for them.
findings.implementation_impact: Existing Phase 1/2 invocations for flashlight and scenario break, or keep working without their config, depending on the developer's choice.
findings.suggestion: State that for every layer, `--config` is a ps-run-layer flag that is forwarded unchanged to each child, and that ps-run-layer itself never derives `--versions` from it. List the run-phases.md command change for Layers 2/5.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Plan ('`all_reuse` keeps today's computation and is informational only')
findings.issue: Today's all_reuse is computed from per-layer `reuse`, which for e2e reads `<module>-e2e-<ver>.json`. The contract stops writing those files and makes `per_version[ver].layers.e2e` a browser-keyed map. 'Today's computation' therefore no longer has its inputs, and the per-version `rerun` list cannot be derived from `layers[l]['reuse']` for e2e.
findings.implementation_impact: The developer has to decide what all_reuse and `per_version[ver].rerun` mean for e2e.
findings.suggestion: Define it: e.g. 'e2e counts as rerun in `rerun`/all_reuse when any configured cell of that version has a rerun_matrix entry'.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Aggregate ('reason as in the plan, `stale-fail` for a stale fail')
findings.issue: `stale-fail` exists only in the aggregate, and its trigger is unclear. A stale record is never gate-grade, so 'newest gate-grade record is a stale fail' cannot happen. Is it the newest record overall being a stale `fail`, the newest cold full conclusive record, or does it replace the plan's `stale-source`/`stale-tag` in that case?
findings.implementation_impact: The aggregate and plan reason vocabularies drift, and tests cannot pin the value.
findings.suggestion: Define it exactly: e.g. 'when the plan reason is stale-source or stale-tag and the cell is failing (newest cold full conclusive record is fail), the aggregate reports stale-fail'. Or add the same reason to the plan.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Scenario prerequisites ('a spec whose effective name equals another spec's ... is skipped with a note naming both files')
findings.issue: With two specs sharing a name, it is unclear whether both are skipped or only the one that sorts later. The rule as written applies symmetrically to both.
findings.implementation_impact: The set of valid specs, and so the full scenario set, authored_assertions and not-gradeable, depends on the reading.
findings.suggestion: Say 'both are skipped' (safer, symmetric) or 'the later one in file-name order is skipped'.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Aggregate (`not_run_cells`) and > Headless (return gains `not_run_cells`)
findings.issue: The shape of `not_run_cells` is not given (a list of "<ver>:<browser>"? objects with reason? only fail-fast not-run, or also no-slots and cells never reached?).
findings.implementation_impact: Headless callers and tests cannot rely on the field.
findings.suggestion: Give the shape, e.g. `[{"cell": "<ver>:<browser>", "reason": "..."}]`, and say which states it includes.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Docs to update at implementation
findings.issue: docs/psm/README.md is missing from the list. It documents the psm config keys in a table (line 57, psm_e2e_browsers) and twice describes cross-version concurrency as `ps-run-layer.py --jobs` (lines 84, 89, 355), which becomes an input error for layer e2e. The new keys psm_e2e_canary, psm_e2e_slots and psm_e2e_warm_ttl do not appear there.
findings.implementation_impact: User-facing docs will contradict the shipped behaviour.
findings.suggestion: Add docs/psm/README.md (config table, --jobs vs --slots for E2E) to the update list.

findings.location: SPEC.md > CAP-1 intent ('The gate (Phase 2) starts only after every version is clean on Layers 1, 2, and 5 and the canary has passing gate-grade evidence') vs cell-contract.md > Plan > Phase 2 entry
findings.issue: The SPEC sets a stricter condition than the contract. The contract also starts Phase 2 when e2e_step is `done` or any step that ends the E2E loop (blocked-by-scope, blocked-not-gradeable, blocked-infra, e2e skipped, psm_e2e_enabled false), and when the canary is not-gradeable. In all of these the canary lacks passing gate-grade evidence.
findings.implementation_impact: A developer who reads the SPEC literally would never enter Phase 2 for a smoke-only module, or when Docker or Playwright is absent.
findings.suggestion: Reword CAP-1 to 'starts after every version is clean on Layers 1, 2, 5 and the plan's e2e_step is gate, done, or a step that ends the E2E loop (cell-contract.md > Phase 2 entry)'.

findings.location: SPEC.md > Constraints ('A source patch still stales every version through mtime') vs cell-contract.md > State, freshness ('source_fingerprint ... File mtime of the record is not used')
findings.issue: E2E freshness is now a content fingerprint that excludes `.git/`, top-level `.psm-*` and `.memlog.md`, while Layers 1/2/5 keep mtime via newest_source_mtime, which excludes vendor/node_modules but not `.psm-*`. So editing `.psm-develop-plan.json` stales Layers 1/2/5 (phase1_reuse false) while E2E stays fresh. The SPEC's 'through mtime' no longer describes E2E, and it is unclear whether `.memlog.md` is excluded only at top level or anywhere.
findings.implementation_impact: There are two staleness rules with different exclusion sets, and Phase 1 loops reopen on a bookkeeping edit while E2E does not. The developer may 'fix' one to match the other.
findings.suggestion: Reword the constraint to 'a source patch still stales every version (E2E: fingerprint; other layers: mtime)'. State whether Layers 1/2/5 should adopt the same exclusions, and whether `.memlog.md` is top-level only.

findings.location: SPEC.md > Why / Open Questions (source: 'takes all day')
findings.issue: The load-bearing pain in the source is wall-clock ('takes all day'), but no done-criterion measures a reduction. CAP-6 only records timings, and the budget is an Open Question. Nothing testable checks that the delivered design actually shortens a validation compared with today's ~18 h bankwire baseline.
findings.implementation_impact: The work can pass every criterion and still not cut the wait. There is nothing to accept against.
findings.suggestion: Add a measurable acceptance item: e.g. a bankwire clean-module run in which total E2E boots ≤ 4 and a warm iteration's wall_clock is below X% of a cold canary run, using CAP-6 data. Or keep it open but state that acceptance is boot-count based.

findings.location: SPEC.md > Assumptions ('canary defaults to the newest target (9.1) × Chromium'); source 'Run version 9 + Chrome first'
findings.issue: Budi named version 9. The default is 'newest of psm_target_versions', so once 10.x is added to the targets the canary silently moves off 9. The source also says 'Chrome', while the spec uses Playwright Chromium (Playwright can drive branded Chrome via channel). The spec notes the assumption but does not say that Chromium-for-Chrome is intended.
findings.implementation_impact: Small drift from the request, which the operator may only notice later.
findings.suggestion: Confirm in the Assumptions that 'newest target' (not literally 9) and Chromium (not branded Chrome) are what Budi meant, or default psm_e2e_canary to `9.1:chromium` in PSM_DEFAULTS.

findings.location: SPEC.md > Success signal ('On bankwire, once the canary has a recorded failure and a warm keeper is up ...'); cell-contract.md tests/live
findings.issue: The live bankwire success-signal test needs the canary to have a recorded failure, but bankwire is expected to be clean, and no fault-injection method is specified (which patch, how it is reverted, whether it runs on a copy of the module).
findings.implementation_impact: The developer has to invent a fault injection that may modify the real module under modules/.
findings.suggestion: Specify that the live test copies bankwire to a temp dir and injects a known failing change (e.g. break one expect_text in a spec or a template string), then applies a one-line fix.
